diagnostic_evidence.quote: For a general variational problem, its multisymplectic form may be defined on the total prolongation space.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper claims that any vertically closed $(p-1,2)$-form $\omega$ can be written in the standard form (eq:multiform). That standard form only allows shifted variables $S_i^{-1}u^{\alpha}$ paired with unshifted $u^{\beta}$ and coefficients $f_{\alpha\beta}^i(\mbn,\mbu)$. But general $(p-1,2)$-forms are defined with arbitrary multi-indices $\mbJ$ in the vertical basis forms $\dv u^{\alpha}_{\mbJ}$ (eq:klform). For example, with $p=1,q=1$, the vertically closed form $\dv u_0\wedge\dv u_1$ cannot be written as $f(n,u_{-1})\,\dv u_{-1}\wedge\dv u_0$. Thus the converse argument does not apply to arbitrary multisymplectic forms.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the converse statement to forms that are already given in the standard form (eq:multiform), or add conditions on the shifts and coefficients that ensure such a representation.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that every multisymplectic P$\Delta$E can be represented by standard multisymplectic forms is false; the converse construction from an arbitrary $\omega$ to standard $\kappa^i$ and hence to a Lagrangian is not justified.
issues.title: General (p-1,2)-form not always in standard multisymplectic form
issues.why_classification: The repair is a localized restriction of a converse claim; the forward direction and main theory remain intact, but the advertised generality is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: However, these equations may be weaker than the given system and so admit other solutions.

issues.failure_explanation: The construction only proves that solutions of the original multisymplectic system satisfy the Euler-Lagrange equations of the constructed $\msL$, i.e. $\mcE^{\vartriangle}(\msL)=0$ on solutions. It does not prove the converse implication, so the Euler-Lagrange equations may be weaker and admit additional solutions. The paper itself notes this caveat in the differential case but omits it here. The subsequent converse existence claim for linear systems is also stated without proof.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the claim to say that the original system implies the Euler-Lagrange equations, and add the caveat that the Lagrangian may admit additional solutions, as in the differential case.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised method to obtain an equivalent Lagrangian from a multisymplectic structure is not established; only a one-way implication is proved.
issues.title: Reconstructed Lagrangian not shown to be equivalent to the system
issues.why_classification: The repair is a limited weakening of the advertised equivalence; it does not require new proof architecture, but it removes a substantive guarantee.
